3. The short fact of the plaintiffs suit is that the land described in the schedule was finally published in RS Khatian No. 291 in the name of Anu Mia being an owner of the properties. Anu Mia sold 44 decimals of land to Ashu Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered deed No. 724 dated 31-1-1954 and plaintiff obtained total 581/3 decimals of land and plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit land. The defendants have no right, title and interest in claiming the land of the plaintiff. On 19-9-1997 while the defendants denied to partition the suit land from the jote then the cause of action arose and the plaintiffs were constrained to file the instant suit. 

 8. Mr Hasan Foez Siddique with Mr Nurul Islam Matubber and Mr Munshi Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsels appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners, submits at the very outset that the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court mainly on 3 grounds. 1. The plaintiffs did not bring all the properties and the schedule of Hotchpot. 2. There are several parties in the jote jointly owning and possessing the suit land but they were not made parties, as such, the suit is bad for defect of parties and 3. There are tanks situated in Khatian Nos. 202 and 291 and there are as many as 200 shares in those tanks who were not made parties. The learned appellate Court observed in his judgment that the plaintiff ought to have sought joint possession but the plaintiff did not seek joint possession in the tank in assailing the judgment of the appellate Court. The learned Counsel further submits that this is nothing but a misreading by the learned Additional District Judge and Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong but, as a matter of fact, the plaintiff sought joint possession in the tanks and drew attention of the Court. The learned Counsel next submits that the properties of Khatian Nos. 202, 291 and 256 were not brought into Hotchpot as because the properties were not disputed, as such, plaintiff did not feel any necessity to bring those properties in the schedule of Hotchpot. There is no legal bar and no suit can fail by reason merely on non-joinder of parties under Order I, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He also submits that the law is also relaxable in a suit for partition that all the joint property should be included in the schedule of properties. The learned Counsel, in support of his contention, relied in the case of Safaruddin vs Fazlul Hug reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151. The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate Court without considering and without applying his judicial mind reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which is not at all sustainable in law because in the suit for partition the defect of parties and hotchpotch of the partition suit will not defeat the suit. This is a mere technical defect for which the suit will not be defeated.  11. He further submits that the properties of Khatian No. 291 Plot No. 109, the properties of Khatian No. 202 Plot Nos. 124, 125 and 131 and also properties of Khatian No. 256 Plot No. 147 were not brought into hotchpotch and not even in the schedule of the suit properties. He also submits that the plaintiffs sought for Saham of 44 decimal of land in the first schedule as per 1/3 share of his predecessor but, as a matter of fact, as per 1/3 shares the plaintiffs were supposed to get 22 decimals of the suit properties but the trial Court, without calculating the quantum of land merely on the basis of surmise and claim of the plaintiffs, gave Saham of 44 decimals of land and passed the decree in favour of the plaintiff and thereby acted illegally which is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the lower appellate Court was absolutely right and justified in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, inasmuch as not considering the defect of parties and hotchpotch of the suit land. Although the learned Advocate for the petitioner tried to advance his argument that the properties of undisputed khatian and the co-sharer of undisputed khatian if not made parties that will not defeat the suit but, as a matter of fact, this will prejudice other co-sharers.
